items.title: Lysosomal protein transmembrane 5 protects against myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury by promoting mitophagy via the NEDD4-LC3 axis.
items.abstract: Mitophagy is essential for mitochondrial quality control during myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury. Lysosomal protein transmembrane 5 (LAPTM5) has been implicated in cardiovascular disease and autophagy, but its role in cardiac mitophagy remains unclear. LAPTM5 knockout mice and cardiomyocyte-targeted AAV9-cTnT-LAPTM5 were used to determine the role of LAPTM5 in myocardial I/R injury. Cardiomyocyte hypoxia/reoxygenation models, mt-Keima imaging, mitochondrial fractionation, LC3-mitochondrial colocalization, co-immunoprecipitation, molecular docking, site-directed mutagenesis, NEDD4 gain- and loss-of-function, and p62 ubiquitination assays were used to investigate the underlying mechanism. Depending on data distribution and group number, appropriate parametric or non-parametric statistics were applied together with correction for multiple testing. LAPTM5 expression progressively decreased following I/R or H/R stress. LAPTM5 deficiency aggravated myocardial injury, cardiac dysfunction, and mitochondrial structural and functional damage, whereas LAPTM5 overexpression attenuated these abnormalities. LAPTM5 promoted mitophagy by enhancing LC3 recruitment to mitochondria. Mechanistically, LAPTM5 recruited NEDD4 to mitochondria through its PY3 motif and facilitated NEDD4-LC3 complex formation. NEDD4 depletion abolished LAPTM5-mediated mitophagy and cytoprotection, whereas re-expression of NEDD4-WT, but not the E3-inactive NEDD4-CS mutant, restored these effects. NEDD4-WT also increased p62 ubiquitination. AAV9-mediated LAPTM5 re-expression reduced infarct size, improved cardiac function, and preserved mitochondrial integrity in LAPTM5-deficient hearts. LAPTM5 protects against myocardial I/R injury by promoting mitophagy through the NEDD4-LC3 axis. PY3-dependent recruitment of NEDD4 and its E3 ubiquitin ligase activity facilitate LC3-associated mitochondrial clearance, accompanied by enhanced p62 ubiquitination, thereby preserving mitochondrial homeostasis during reperfusion.

items.title: A Triple-Functional Nanoplatform for Oxidative Stress-Driven Pressure Ulcer Therapy.
items.abstract: Pressure ulcers (PUs) are chronic wounds driven by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, impaired angiogenesis, and delayed remodeling, yet current treatments remain suboptimal. Here, we developed a novel nanocomposite (CCH) by loading cerium oxide (CeO 2 ) and curcumin into hollow mesoporous silica nanoparticles (HMSN). CCH exhibited well-defined spherical morphology, favorable particle size, and pH-dependent drug release. Mechanistically, CCH possessed potent superoxide dismutase (SOD)- and catalase (CAT)-mimetic activities, effectively scavenging reactive oxygen species. In vitro, CCH was efficiently internalized by HUVECs, showed excellent biocompatibility up to 100 μg/mL, protected HUVECs from oxidative damage by reducing intracellular ROS and restoring VEGF secretion, and induced anti-inflammatory M2 macrophage polarization. In a mouse model of pressure ulcer, topical CCH application significantly accelerated wound closure, enhanced re-epithelialization and granulation tissue formation, reduced systemic CRP and PCT levels, and improved scar prognosis, associated with increased VEGF expression and CD31-positive vascularization, along with organized collagen deposition. Collectively, CCH integrates antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, pro-angiogenic, and tissue-remodeling functions into a single nanoplatform, effectively addressing key pathological features of PUs. Thus, CCH represents a promising and safe candidate for chronic wound management.

items.title: Left atrial appendage occlusion for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation: recent evidence, catheter ablation, and future trials.
items.abstract: Oral anticoagulation (OAC) remains the standard for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF), but bleeding, non-persistence and thromboembolism despite treatment create important unmet needs. Catheter ablation and left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) address distinct mechanisms and do not reproduce systemic anticoagulation. This narrative review covers randomized anticoagulation-withdrawal studies after ablation, trials and pooled evidence on LAAO, patients unable to sustain anticoagulation, procedural imaging and healing, post-implant antithrombotic therapy, and future trial design. Targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE and ClinicalTrials.gov were supplemented by citation screening and review of contemporary congress reports, for evidence spanning 2005-10 October 2026. The completed randomized LAAO programme mainly tests substitution where OAC remains feasible. Precision source control should be investigated as rescue when OAC cannot be sustained and as a potential dose-sparing complement in selected patients, while addressing residual ischemic risk and verifying durable closure.

items.title: Work-time arrangements, career progression, and job satisfaction among physicians in Germany: a cross-sectional survey.
items.abstract: Demographic change and evolving expectations regarding work-life balance are increasingly challenging the medical workforce in Germany. Work-time arrangements play a key role in physician job satisfaction, well-being, and career development. However, part-time and alternative working models remain unevenly implemented and are frequently perceived as limiting career opportunities. This study characterized current work-time arrangements among physicians in Germany and examined satisfaction, employer support, colleague acceptance, perceived career opportunities, barriers to reducing working hours, and work-family balance. This cross-sectional study is based on an anonymous digital survey conducted by the German Medical Women's Association between September 2022 and July 2023. Physicians across medical specialties and career stages were invited to participate. The questionnaire assessed sociodemographic and professional characteristics, work-time arrangements (full-time, part-time, and alternative models), satisfaction with current arrangements, employer support, and perceived career opportunities. Of the 898 respondents, 90.9% were women and 46.2% were resident physicians. Full-time employment was the most common arrangement (56.8%). Physicians working in non-full-time arrangements were more frequently satisfied with their work-time arrangement than those working full-time (52.8% vs. 45.3%; p = 0.020). Hospital-based physicians were less likely to be satisfied with their work-time arrangement (aOR 0.33) or to receive support from their employer in implementing alternative work-time arrangements (aOR 0.24). They were also less likely to report acceptance of alternative work-time arrangements among colleagues (aOR 0.21) and equal career opportunities under such arrangements (aOR 0.31), while being more likely to report difficulties balancing work and family responsibilities (aOR 2.44; all p < 0.001). Compared with physicians in leadership positions, resident physicians and board-certified physicians without leadership responsibility reported lower satisfaction and lower perceived equal career opportunities, while reporting greater difficulty balancing work and family responsibilities (all p < 0.001). Fear of negative career consequences was the most frequently reported reason for not reducing working hours (58.2%), and approximately two thirds of respondents perceived unequal career opportunities for colleagues using alternative work-time arrangements. Although full-time employment remained the most common arrangement, respondents not working full-time reported greater satisfaction. Part-time and alternative work-time-arrangements are widely perceived as career-limiting. Addressing structural barriers and ensuring equal career opportunities for physicians who require or prefer family-friendly working conditions are essential for physician well-being, workforce retention, and the long-term resilience of healthcare systems.

items.title: Persistent pocket-site pain after cardiac implantable electronic device implantation: a prospective observational study of prevalence, neuropathic characteristics, and quality of life.
items.abstract: Although transvenous cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) implantation is generally considered a minor procedure, long-lasting pocket-site pain may represent an underrecognized clinical problem. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence, characteristics, and clinical impact of persistent pain after CIED implantation. This prospective observational study included patients who underwent first-time CIED implantation and attended routine outpatient follow-up visits. Pain intensity was assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), and neuropathic pain characteristics were evaluated using the Douleur Neuropathique 4 Questions (DN-4) questionnaire. Health-related quality of life was assessed using the Short Form-12 (SF-12). Demographic and clinical data were also recorded. A total of 102 patients were included in the analysis. Persistent implantation-site pain (VAS ≥ 4) was reported by 22.5% of patients. Neuropathic pain characteristics (DN-4 ≥ 4) were identified in 26.5% of patients. A moderate positive correlation was observed between VAS and DN-4 scores (ρ = 0.473, p < 0.001). However, the association between VAS ≥ 4 and DN-4 ≥ 4 was not statistically significant and had a small effect size (p = 0.118; φ = 0.15). Pain intensity was moderately negatively correlated with the SF-12 physical component score, indicating reduced physical quality of life with increasing pain severity, while mental quality of life was not significantly affected. Persistent pocket-site pain after CIED implantation affected a clinically meaningful proportion of patients despite generally low overall pain scores. Higher DN-4 scores were associated with poorer physical and mental quality of life and may provide additional clinical information in selected patients. However, because the categorical association between VAS-defined persistent pain and DN-4 positivity was not statistically significant, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in larger prospective studies.

items.title: FASN as a Therapeutic Target in Genitourinary Diseases: From Cancers to Benign Disorders.
items.abstract: Fatty acid synthase (FASN) is the key catalytic enzyme of de novo lipogenesis and is increasingly recognized as a driver of metabolic reprogramming in genitourinary disease. In both malignant and non-malignant settings, aberrant FASN expression and activity are associated with tumor growth, metastatic spread, drug resistance, renal lipotoxicity, fibrosis, and immune remodeling. However, current evidence remains scattered across organ-specific studies, and a focused synthesis across the genitourinary system is still lacking. This review summarizes the expression patterns, upstream regulators, downstream effects, and translational relevance of FASN in major genitourinary organs, with emphasis on the bladder, kidney, prostate, cervix, and ovary, as well as selected benign disorders. We also review current therapeutic strategies, including direct FASN inhibition, modulation of upstream lipogenic pathways, nanodelivery approaches, and rational combination regimens with chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, or immunotherapy. Available data support FASN as a shared metabolic node linking lipid reprogramming to both malignant progression and organ injury. In bladder, renal, prostate, and cervical cancers, FASN contributes to proliferation, invasion, metastasis, and treatment resistance. In renal and reproductive disorders, it is also involved in lipid deposition, inflammation, fibrosis, and ovulatory dysfunction. Despite promising preclinical findings, major challenges remain, including limited evidence in benign disease, marked mechanistic heterogeneity across organs, and insufficient clinical validation of biomarkers and targeted agents. A more integrated understanding of FASN may improve biomarker development and support metabolism-based precision therapy in genitourinary disease.

items.title: From cytoreduction to precision oncology: evolution of ovarian cancer therapy.
items.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the most lethal gynecologic malignancy due to its asymptomatic progression, limited screening modalities, and late-stage diagnosis. Although initial responses to platinum-based chemotherapy are common, recurrence and multidrug resistance are nearly universal, necessitating a shift toward biomarker-guided, precision-based interventions. This review synthesizes current evidence on the evolving landscape of ovarian cancer treatment, with emphasis on molecular pathogenesis, histotype-specific vulnerabilities, and advances in therapeutic strategies. Focus is placed on the clinical integration of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-targeting agents, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and antibody-drug conjugates, alongside emerging platforms such as liquid biopsy, artificial intelligence-enhanced diagnostics, and histotype-driven targeted therapies. Translational insights from other malignancies were utilized to highlight future directions for ovarian cancer, including dual pathway targeting, immune and epigenetic modulation, and receptor-guided cytotoxic delivery. Collectively, these advances demonstrate how precision oncology is advancing ovarian cancer treatment, with the potential to improve survival outcomes while preserving quality of life.

items.title: Synergistic nanotheranostic platform for fluorescence/magnetic resonance bimodal imaging-guided near infrared photoimmuno-chemodynamic thermal targeting therapy.
items.abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) photoimmunotherapy (PIT) is a promising cancer treatment strategy involving antibody-photoabsorber conjugates. However, the imaging depth and photobleaching susceptibility of the IR700 fluorescence used for treatment monitoring are limited, and antigen heterogeneity within tumors compromises the efficacy of strictly antigen-restricted therapies. We developed a synergistic nanotheranostic platform that integrates NIR-PIT, photothermal therapy, and chemodynamic therapy (CDT) into a single MRI-visible agent (NIR-PICT 3 ). To achieve NIR-PICT 3 , conjugation of mAb-IRDye700DX (mAb-IR700) to dextran-coated superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (nanomag-D-spio) yielded nanomag-D-spio-mAb-IR700, enabling dual imaging (IR700 fluorescence/MRI) and targeted cytotoxicity upon 690-nm irradiation. The conjugate retained antigen selectivity, exhibited activatable NIR fluorescence after cellular uptake, generated negative T1- and T2-weighted MRI contrast, and demonstrated robust, cycle-enhanced photothermal performance. Iron-mediated redox catalysis promoted ·OH generation, supporting CDT. In vivo, systemic administration led to marked tumor accumulation, as confirmed by multimodal analyses. Repeated light dosing exploited the NIR-PIT-induced super-enhanced permeability and retention (SUPR) effect, enhancing nanoparticle retention, tumor heating, and therapeutic efficacy. In EGFR+ xenografts, NIR-PICT 3 achieved superior tumor regression and survival while inducing photothermal bystander effects in antigen-heterogeneous models. These results establish a modular, image-guided strategy for platform therapy to overcome monitoring depth limitations and antigen heterogeneity in solid tumor NIR-PIT.

items.title: Naringin promotes cancer immunity by inducing cross-presentation by antigen-presenting cells.
items.abstract: Successful immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) treatment of cancer requires adequate infiltration of cytotoxic CD8+T lymphocytes (CTLs) in tumors. Previous studies have identified the compound naringin, which increases CTL infiltration and rescues ICI efficacy in CTL-lacking tumors, and cancer CTL priming has been shown to rely on antigen cross-presentation (XPT). Therefore, the present study aimed to examine the effect of naringin on XPT by various human and murine antigen-presenting cells (APCs). The results indicated that naringin increases XPT by XPT-competent APCs, including murine bone marrow (BM) dendritic cells, peritoneal macrophages (MΦs), and human monocyte-derived dendritic cells (HMDCs). However, XPT was not observed with BM- or human monocyte-derived MΦs with or without naringin. Naringin reduced the activity of lysosomes, suppressing the degradation of internalized antigens, thereby increasing antigen cytosolic escape and MHC class I molecule-presenting antigens. In addition, human lymph node (LN) sinus MΦs were transcriptomically more similar to XPT-competent HMDCs than other LN MΦ groups. Taken together, these data suggest that naringin promotes XPT by XPT-competent APCs, which may explain why naringin was found to promote cancer immunity in our previous studies. This finding highlights the potential for developing cancer immunotherapies that induce XPT, offering a promising strategy to enhance antitumor immune responses.

items.title: Precision oncology in advanced melanoma: molecular landscapes and personalized therapy recommendations from the Molecular Tumor Board Freiburg.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and BRAF/MEK kinase inhibitors have substantially improved survival in advanced melanoma; however, therapeutic resistance and severe toxicities underscore the ongoing need for alternative strategies. Here, we evaluate the clinical utility of multi-omic profiling, biomarker-stratified recommendations, and survival outcomes within a prospective cohort of 98 patients with advanced cutaneous or uveal melanoma evaluated by the Molecular Tumor Board Freiburg (MTB-FR) between 2021 and 2024. Completed profiling revealed at least one potential actionable target beyond classical BRAF V600 mutations in 83.8% of cases. Alterations in NRAS, atypical BRAF variants, CDK4/6 pathway amplifications, and DNA-damage response (DDR) gene mutations most frequently guided board recommendations. Biomarker-stratified therapies were recommended for 68.4% of patients, and personalized immunotherapy combinations for 72.4%. The treatment implementation rate was 33.8% (n = 27), achieving an overall disease control rate (DCR) of 42.9% and an overall response rate (ORR) of 10.7%. These findings demonstrate that comprehensive molecular profiling in a real-world setting uncovers actionable alterations, providing viable subsequent treatment avenues that may optimize outcomes for heavily pretreated melanoma patients beyond established standards of care. Ultimately, prospective, randomized, biomarker-driven trials remain essential to validate whether these individualized diagnostic strategies translate into a reproducible survival benefit.

items.title: Protective mechanisms against murine coronavirus infection in individual mice and its transmission between mice.
items.abstract: Murine coronavirus, commonly known as mouse hepatitis virus (MHV), is a representative pathogenic virus in mice. MHV infection in mice is used as a model for viral infections and is utilized to analyze the mechanisms of protection and transmission. By establishing MHV-specific T cell clones and conducting adoptive transfer experiments in infected mice, it was demonstrated that T cells play a crucial role in the protection against MHV infection and that cytotoxic T lymphocytes induce apoptosis in infected cells and suppress viral production. Furthermore, studies using IFN-γ-deficient C57BL/6 mice demonstrated exacerbation of acute hepatitis, establishment of persistent viral infection, and subsequent death due to subacute granulomatous serositis resembling feline infectious peritonitis in cats, possibly in association with persistent infection and the emergence of immune-escape variants. In contrast, all MHV-infected IFN-γ-deficient BALB/c mice died within a short period due to acute fulminant hepatitis, indicating that genetic background differences significantly influence disease progression. Furthermore, in vitro studies demonstrated that BALB/c mouse hepatocytes are more susceptible to MHV than C57BL/6 mouse hepatocytes. Additionally, the mode of transmission of MHV was experimentally analyzed, and clearly correlated with viral growth in the intestine. Other studies have explored a wide range of topics in relation to MHV infection, including autoimmune responses, genetic susceptibility, and the maintenance of pluripotency in MHV-infected embryonic stem cells. MHV has also been utilized as a surrogate virus for COVID-19 research.

items.title: HBIG-free strategies after liver transplantation: is hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence the missing piece?
Hepatitis B screening among asylum seekers: a retrospective cohort study in Modena, Northern Italy.
items.abstract: Hepatitis B virus remains a major health challenge among migrants from high-endemic regions arriving in low-endemic countries like Italy. However, more evidence on both infection burden and immunity gaps among asylum seekers is needed to inform prevention policies. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 739 asylum seekers screened for Hepatitis B virus (HBV) in Modena, Northern Italy, between 2019 and 2023. Serological testing included quantitative determination of HBsAg, HBcAb, and HBsAb, allowing identification of active infection, natural immunity, vaccine-induced immunity, and susceptibility. Demographic characteristics, geographic origin, and migration routes were analyzed in relation to HBV status. Participants were predominantly male (94.7%), with a mean age of 27.2 years, and originated mainly from South Asia (59.4%) and Sub-Saharan Africa (26.1%). Overall HBsAg prevalence was 4.1%, substantially higher than what reported for the Italian general population (<1%). Prevalence was highest among Sub-Saharan African migrants (7.3%), who also showed the greatest proportion of natural immunity (36.3%), while South Asian migrants had a prevalence of 3.6% and Northern African migrants null. Among HBsAg-negative individuals, 57% were susceptible to HBV infection, particularly those from South Asia and Northern Africa. Susceptibility was associated with male sex (OR 4.08, 95% CI 1.34-12.44) and age ≥25 years (OR 2.38, 95% CI 1.40-4.04), consistent with birth before the introduction of universal HBV vaccination in many countries. Most HBsAg-positive individuals reported transit through Libya. Asylum seekers in Italy show a high prevalence of HBV infection alongside substantial immunity deficits. Systematic screening and targeted catch-up vaccination should be prioritized within migrant health services as a key public health intervention.

items.title: Equitable outcomes for critically urgent living donor liver transplantation in acute alcoholic hepatitis.
items.abstract: The justification for living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) for acute alcoholic hepatitis (AAH) remains debated, particularly in urgent settings. We compared outcomes of recipients undergoing urgent LDLT for AAH versus other causes and identified predictors of mortality. We analyzed 317 adults in the Korean national registry who underwent urgent LDLT from 2017 to 2021 within seven days of emergency approval. AAH was defined using National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism criteria, excluding coexisting liver disease. Recipient, donor, and perioperative variables were compared between the AAH (n = 114) and non-alcoholic groups (n = 203). Survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis, and predictors of death using Cox regression. AAH recipients had more severe decompensation, particularly hepatorenal syndrome and ascites. One-, two-, and three-year survival rates were 90.1%, 86.5%, and 86.5% in the AAH group versus 83.1%, 79.6%, and 77.9% in the non-alcoholic group (log-rank p = 0.321). Overall, 66 recipients (20. 8%) died. Pretransplant ventilator support (hazard ratio [HR] 1.954), donor age ≥ 55 years (HR 3.134), and chronic kidney disease independently predicted mortality, whereas AAH did not (HR 0.765, 95% confidence interval 0.440-1.329; p = 0.341). AAH did not independently predict mortality following urgent LDLT. Instead, outcomes were influenced by the recipient's pre-surgery condition and the characteristics of the donor and graft, suggesting that the procedure is justified when candidates are carefully selected.

items.title: Impact of nationwide parvovirus B19 DNA screening and identification of transfusion-transmitted infections.
items.abstract: Parvovirus B19 (B19V) testing is often not required to release blood components. However, the European Pharmacopoeia requires that plasma pools for fractionation contain no more than 10 4  IU/mL of B19V DNA. In France, pool B19 nucleic acid testing (NAT) screening was performed by Établissement Français du Sang since 2015. Since June 2024, positive pools are broken down into individual testing, allowing for the identification and management of infected blood donations. B19V NAT is performed in pools of 96 donations (P96) with the DPX Parvo/hepatitis A virus assay (Roche). A P96 with a viral load >10 4  IU/mL B19V DNA is considered positive. All individual donations (IDs) testing reactive for B19V by ID-NAT are excluded from plasma-based medicinal products production, and the corresponding blood components are destroyed if not yet transfused. From June 2024 to June 2025, 99 of 2,627,678 donations (3.7/100,000) were B19V DNA positive. All blood components related to 90 donations were discarded. Of the remaining nine donations, 13 blood components (9 platelet concentrates [PCs] that had undergone pathogen reduction (PR) and four red blood cell [RBC] concentrates) were transfused before NAT results were obtained. Two B19V transmissions were reported in recipients (0.078/100,000 transfusions) after transfusion of 1 PR-PC and 1 RBC unit. B19V DNA testing for plasma intended for fractionation performed in blood services helps in avoiding transmissions by the related blood components, provided positive donations are detected prior to their transfusion. Delayed availability of results may result in transfusion-transmitted B19V infection, which cannot prevented by current PR technology.

items.title: Decoding metabolic diseases through bacterial extracellular vesicles: mechanisms, diagnostics, and therapeutics.
items.abstract: Metabolic diseases represent a class of chronic conditions characterized by disturbances in energy and material metabolism. These diseases primarily include obesity, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, atherosclerosis, type 2 diabetes, osteoporosis, and polycystic ovary syndrome. A core pathological feature underlying their development is the mutual reinforcement between chronic low-grade inflammation and metabolic imbalance. The gut microbiota has been highlighted by recent research as a key regulator of host metabolism, while bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs) are emerging as critical mediators. BEVs transport bioactive molecules (proteins, lipids, nucleic acids) to facilitate microbiota-host crosstalk without direct contact. Pathogen-derived BEVs often exacerbate metabolic dysfunction via inflammation, while commensal/probiotic BEVs protect against disorders by enhancing intestinal barrier function and regulating immunity. Furthermore, owing to their high stability, easy penetration of biological barriers, and capacity to carry abundant cellular information, BEVs demonstrate broad application prospects as non-invasive diagnostic biomarkers for metabolic diseases and as natural or engineered targeted drug delivery vehicles. This review outlines the mechanisms and progress in the application of gut BEVs in metabolic diseases. It aims to deepen our understanding of host-microbiota interaction networks and support the development of novel intervention strategies for metabolic diseases.

items.title: LINC00907 suppresses malignant progression in hepatocellular carcinoma by inhibiting miR-24-3p.
items.abstract: This study aimed to clarify the role of LINC00907 in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and its underlying molecular mechanisms. The research population comprised 117 participants diagnosed with HCC. The expressions of LINC00907 and miR-24-3p in both tissue specimens and cell lines, along with those of EMT markers and the MMP-2 and MMP-9, were measured using RT-qPCR. Cellular proliferation was measured with the CCK-8 assay, while apoptotic rates were determined by flow cytometry. The direct interactions between LINC00907, miR-24-3p, and PDGFRL were validated by dual luciferase reporter and RNA pull-down assays. HCC cells were transfected with constructs specifically modulating LINC00907 and miR-24-3p to investigate the impact of their expression on malignant phenotypic behaviors. LINC00907 expression was significantly downregulated in HCC, whereas miR-24-3p expression was upregulated. Low LINC00907 expression was linked to significantly worse overall survival, as determined by Kaplan-Meier analysis. The upregulation of LINC00907 led to the suppression of cell proliferation and EMT, while inducing apoptosis and reducing the levels of MMP-2 and MMP-9. LINC00907 was shown to directly target and negatively regulate miR-24-3p. Furthermore, rescue experiments demonstrated that upregulation of miR-24-3p counteracted the tumor-suppressive effects mediated by LINC00907 overexpression in HCC cells. LINC00907 exerts tumor-suppressive effects by targeting and negatively regulating miR-24-3p, thereby influencing proliferation, apoptosis, and EMT in HCC cells.

items.title: Sleep disorders as an emerging risk factor for liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies.
items.abstract: Sleep disorders are increasingly recognized as contributors to metabolic dysfunction and chronic liver disease, but their associations with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and cirrhosis remain unclear. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the relationship between sleep disorders and liver-related outcomes. Following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420261342781), we searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library through February 2026 for cohort studies assessing sleep disorders and liver outcomes. Adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) or odds ratios (ORs) were pooled using random-effects models. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed, and risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I. Thirteen cohort studies were included. Overall, sleep disorders were associated with an increased risk of liver-related outcomes (HR 1.49; 95% CI 1.22-1.81; I² = 96%). Insomnia was significantly associated with increased risk (HR 1.39; 95% CI 1.28-1.49), whereas obstructive sleep apnea showed a non-significant trend (HR 1.80; 95% CI 0.91-3.58). Sleep disorders were linked to higher risks of HCC (HR 1.42; 95% CI 1.15-1.77) and unspecified liver cancer (HR 1.26; 95% CI 1.01-1.57), but not cirrhosis. Findings were robust in sensitivity analyses, with no significant publication bias. Sleep disorders, particularly insomnia, are associated with increased risks of HCC and liver-related outcomes. These findings highlight sleep disturbances as potentially modifiable risk factors in liver disease progression.

items.title: Genome-wide analyses identify 60 loci associated with liver triglyceride content.
items.abstract: We performed a large-scale genome-wide association study meta-analysis of magnetic resonance imaging-derived liver triglyceride content across 71,488 European-ancestry participants from the UK Biobank, approximately doubling the sample size of previous genome-wide association studies 1 . We identified 60 independent loci, including 31 not previously reported, and estimated the single nucleotide polymorphism-based heritability of liver triglyceride content at 25%. Integrative fine-mapping and gene-prioritization analyses nominated candidate effector genes for 48 loci. Of the 31 newly identified variants, 14 were validated in meta-analyses of clinically diagnosed metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (42,163 cases and 1,646,254 controls). People in the highest versus lowest decile of a polygenic risk score for liver triglyceride content had 2.71-fold higher odds of cirrhosis and 7.47-fold higher odds of hepatocellular carcinoma. Plasma proteins associated with the liver triglyceride polygenic risk score were enriched for metabolic remodeling and inflammatory pathways, with liver-enriched protein signatures increasing and visceral adipose signatures decreasing with higher genetic risk. Together, these findings refine the genetic architecture of liver triglyceride content, linking polygenic susceptibility to downstream metabolic and inflammatory pathways and providing insights into the genetic basis of steatotic liver disease.

items.title: Spatial transcriptomic sequencing identifies lipid metabolism and mitochondrial respiration as central features of T cell excluded esophageal adenocarcinomas.
items.abstract: The tumour immune microenvironment influences neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy success in esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC). Complete responders show higher treatment-naïve intratumoral CD8+ T cell levels before treatment than non-complete responders. Understanding mechanisms driving CD8+ T cells exclusion from the TIME is essential to improving outcomes. We performed spatial transcriptomics on treatment-naive CD8-low and high EACs (N = 12). Regions of interest (ROIs) were selected based on tumour annotation by a pathologist. Cancer (CK+) cells and immune (CD45+) cells were analysed within the same ROI. Findings were validated using bulk transcriptome data (TCGA) and metabolic profiling (SCENITH) of fresh tumour specimen (n = 5). Whole transcriptomic profiling showed cancer cell clustering based on T cell infiltration. Cancer cell transcriptomes of CD8-low tumours exhibited reduced antigen presentation and upregulated lipid and mitochondrial metabolism, while CD8-high tumours showed increased cytokine signalling and apoptotic pathways. In CD45+ compartments, CD8-low tumours were enriched for the PGC-1α pathway, linked to mitochondrial biogenesis and immunosuppressive myeloid populations. These findings were supported by TCGA data. SCENITH confirmed mitochondrial dependence of macrophages in CD8-low tumours. Our results suggest that mitochondrial metabolism and impaired antigen presentation contribute to T cell exclusion in EAC. These findings raise the hypothesis that targeting mitochondrial metabolism in these cancers can modulate the anti-tumour immune response and thereby improve the response to chemoradiotherapy.
